title: Main Supercuspidal Theta Correspondence Theorem
body_html:
Main Supercuspidal Theta Correspondence Theorem

Let \(\Sigma\) be a supercuspidal datum for \(G=U(V)\), and equip it with the canonical splitting over its compact subgroup in the dual pair, giving a covering datum \(\widetilde\Sigma\). If \[ [\Sigma']=\#_{V,T'}([\Sigma]) \] for a target space \(V'\in T'\), then the first-occurrence local theta lift satisfies \[ \theta_{V,V'}(\widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma}) = \widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma'}. \]

Conversely, if \(\widetilde\pi\) and its theta lift \(\widetilde\pi'\) are both supercuspidal, then \(\widetilde\pi\) is attached to some covering datum \(\widetilde\Sigma\), and \(\widetilde\pi'\) is attached to a covering datum whose underlying ordinary datum lies in \[ \#_{V,T'}([\Sigma]). \] Thus the first-occurrence theta correspondence between tame supercuspidal representations is completely described by the data-level map built from moment maps and finite-field theta lifts.
proof_html:
For the forward direction, start with a covering datum \(\widetilde\Sigma\). The construction of \(\#_{V,T'}\) decomposes \(\Sigma\) into single blocks, transfers each positive-depth block by the moment-map construction, transfers the depth-zero block by finite-field theta correspondence, and then takes the direct sum. This gives a target covering datum \(\widetilde\Sigma'\) and an orbit \(\Omega\) in the generalized lattice model.

Proposition 8.1 computes the relevant \(K\times K'\)-intertwining space in the oscillator representation: \[ \dim\operatorname{Hom}_{K_M}(\eta_M,S(B_0)_\Omega)=1. \] Hence the oscillator representation contains the product of the source \(K\)-type and the contragredient target \(K'\)-type. By compact induction, the theta lift of \(\widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma}\) has a nonzero quotient containing the \(K'\)-type attached to \(\widetilde\Sigma'\). Supercuspidality and irreducibility at first occurrence identify this quotient with \(\widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma'}\).

For the converse, assume that \(\widetilde\pi\) and its theta lift \(\widetilde\pi'\) are both supercuspidal. The exhaustion theorem for covering data writes \(\widetilde\pi\) as \(\widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma}\) for some covering datum. Proposition 9.1 then applies to any supercuspidal target occurrence: after replacing the source datum by an equivalent one, the target contains the \(K'\)-type datum constructed by \(\#_{V,T'}\). The Hakim-Murnaghan equivalence theorem for the corresponding Yu data identifies the target representation with the representation attached to that target covering datum. Therefore the target datum lies in \(\#_{V,T'}([\Sigma])\), as claimed.
